clue.text: Leak in stately home where dukes reside

indicators.note: dukes residing in the home means they are lodged inside it, one set of letters housed within the other

blocks.note: a pile is a grand country house
D is the abbreviation for duke, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A roof is dripping in a grand house where aristocrats live.
explanation.walkthrough: PILE holds DD to make PIDDLE; 'Leak' is the slang noun or verb for passing water, not a roof drip.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a leak is slang for urinating, and piddle is a childish informal word for the same act.

indicators.note: placed among the children means set in the middle of that word

blocks.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants
north and south are the two opposite poles

explanation.surface: Someone observed that a group of children included two complete opposites.
explanation.walkthrough: SEED takes NS in the middle: SE-NS-ED. Seed for children is biblical usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sensed something is to have perceived or become aware of it, a plain synonym.

blocks.note: surface reading: a convenient way of doing things
setter's reading: a show worked by a hand inside a garment, also the name for posing online under fake identities

explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' seems to mean convenient, but it means operated by hand, as a puppet made from a sock is; the same name covers inventing fake accounts to praise yourself online.
explanation.definitionFit: Creating false online personas to support your own views or attack others is known by this term, borrowed from the children's toy.

blocks.note: surface reading: a modest count of something
setter's reading: the short form of number, no., spun round, and also a phrase meaning aroused

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: ON once turned gives NO, the abbreviation for number. That is why the question mark is there.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aroused or enthused by something is described informally as being switched on by it.

indicators.note: one thing coming before another puts its letters first in the answer

blocks.note: out means not permitted, as in smoking is out
a fit is a bout, as of coughing

explanation.surface: Something about stripping being banned ahead of a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip is the British word for a sports team's kit, not undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A team's strip is its set of matching clothes, which is an outfit.

clue.text: Support briefly up - clear about this form of air travel?

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short by its final letter
in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
turned about, the word's letters are moved around into a fresh order

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note about holding something up and clearing space for a way of travelling by air.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK loses its K, then goes up to CAB; CLEAR rearranged gives LECAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable car is a cabin hauled along an overhead wire, so it travels through the air.

clue.text: Before birth of current emperor, quite regularly accepted

indicators.note: taking a word regularly means keeping every other letter of it
the emperor accepting something takes it in among his own letters

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
Nero was a Roman emperor
the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A historical note about the time before a modern emperor was born.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the physics symbol for current; 'quite regularly' wants its even letters, not the odd ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in the womb, describing what happens to a baby before it is born.

clue.text: You originally voiced Mulan, the central part (bit throaty)

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the following word
the central part of a name keeps only its middle letters

blocks.note: U is the text-speak spelling of you, which sounds the same
the opening letter of the word
the middle three letters of the name

explanation.surface: Someone tells an actor they first provided the voice of the Disney heroine Mulan.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvula is the fleshy lobe hanging at the back of the throat, a small piece of throat anatomy.

indicators.note: one word sitting in another is placed inside its letters

blocks.note: ads is short for advertisements
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: Tailors are doing fittings in television adverts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailors' looks like people who make suits; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to modify it to suit a purpose, which is to adapt it.

clue.text: Involved in fetish, finally entices Stef into sexual relations

indicators.note: being involved in something means being wrapped up inside it
finally picks out the last letter of each word that follows

blocks.note: a kink is an unusual sexual preference
the last letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A racy tale of someone with a fetish luring Stef into an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sexual relations' reads as one phrase, but 'sexual' only supplies its last letter and 'relations' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinsfolk are a person's family members, which is what relations means here.

clue.text: After preliminary introduction to ecdysiasts, party got livelier

indicators.note: an introduction to a word is its first letter
the party coming after the other pieces puts it last in the answer

blocks.note: a heat is a preliminary round of a race
the opening letter of the word
the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Once the strippers came on, the party became much livelier.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecdysiasts is a jokey word for striptease artists. Party is not DO here but the Northern Irish DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: When things heat up they become more intense or animated, so a party that heated up got livelier.

indicators.note: one thing cutting another slices into it, ending up inside

blocks.note: pace is rate of movement
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A learner driver is spotted cutting their speed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain learner drivers display an L plate, hence L for learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a location or site, which is a place.

clue.text: Had to work with 21, in short, for free

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, set going in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 21 across, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Someone had to work alongside others without being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for free' looks like unpaid; 'free' is a verb meaning release.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something from what holds it is to detach or unfasten it.

clue.text: Lively for one's age (though needing a shower!)

indicators.note: a word that is needing something lacks it, so that letter is missing

blocks.note: a spray is a shower of fine droplets
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old person is sprightly, if not exactly clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus A would be SPRAY, a shower; so the answer is the shower still needing its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes an elderly person who is still active and nimble.

clue.text: Cheer up - pulling article in support of Prince Harry

indicators.note: pulling something out takes it away from the word
in a down entry, a supporting piece sits below the other

blocks.note: P is an abbreviation for prince
to reassure someone is to cheer them up
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A message of support for the royal Prince Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince Harry' reads as one name; 'Prince' gives P and 'Harry' is the verb definition. REASSURE without its A goes under P.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to harass or press them persistently, which is to put pressure on them.

indicators.note: the head of a word resigning means its first letter quits it

blocks.note: strain is pressure or stress

explanation.surface: A school's head teacher resigns because of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School head' reads as headteacher, but 'School' is the verb definition and 'head' is the first letter of the stress word.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or drill them, which is to train them.

indicators.note: a word picked apart is broken up and its letters reassembled

blocks.note: to tow is to pull or drag
the answer to 27 across

explanation.surface: Taking an enormous drag on a cigarette while picking something apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Towering means very tall or great in size, like a tower, so huge.

blocks.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Asks whether violent bloodshed is something that excites people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-on' reads as something arousing; split it into turn and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore is blood spilt through violence, as in a gory horror film.

indicators.note: once the words have been damaged their letters come out in a broken order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lost their job after damaging a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bin' looks like a noun but is the verb, to throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: To bin something is informal for throwing it away, disposing of it.

indicators.note: a word set back is turned so it runs in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a pen is a writing tool
to hew is to chop or hack

explanation.surface: A hack journalist suffers a setback that relates to their writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' wants to be a poor journalist; it is the verb chop.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a sibling's son, a family member, so a relative.

indicators.note: the books going inside means they are placed within the other word

blocks.note: locks are tresses of hair
OT is the Old Testament, a group of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have locked away some books and is dismissed as all talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' looks like a verb but is the noun for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is empty, boastful talk, which is what bluster is.

clue.text: Spain and Thailand create problem, with some others

indicators.note: the word is made into a problem, scrambled out of its usual order

blocks.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two countries cause a diplomatic problem, with others joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'create' is the anagram fodder, not a verb in the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means and the rest, used to stand for some other unlisted items.

indicators.note: the tail of the word turns round, so its last two letters swap

blocks.note: Castor and Pollux are the twins of Gemini

explanation.surface: A communist with a twin flees the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tail' means running away, but here only the last two letters of the twin's name turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led communist Cuba, so his surname names a famous communist.

clue.text: Right, what remains in use, not for the first time?

definitions.text: in use, not for the first time
definitions.note: a phrase describing a rehash rather than a synonym for it

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
eh? is said when asking what
ash is what remains after a fire

explanation.surface: Talk of recycling leftovers, using them once again.
explanation.walkthrough: R, EH, ASH. The question mark flags that the definition describes the answer rather than equalling it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old material reused with little change, so it is being put to use again.

indicators.note: a disbanded group breaks up and its members scatter into new places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Secret cliques have been broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a select inner circle, so it is private or hidden.

clue.text: Copper wrong about rule - that's the key point

indicators.note: copper going about something wraps around it

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
R is an abbreviation for rule
a cross marks an answer wrong

explanation.surface: A policeman gets a rule wrong, and that is the crucial issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' wants to be a police officer; it is the metal. CU goes about R, then X follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The crux of a matter is its most important or decisive part, the heart of the issue.

indicators.note: one word outside another goes around it

blocks.note: to spot something is to sight it
read as Leather head: the head, or first letter, of leather

explanation.surface: A small spot seen outside the Surrey town of Leatherhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a town in Surrey; split it into Leather and head.
explanation.definitionFit: Slight means small in amount or degree, so little.

clue.text: Are rulers here ignored to some extent?

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Asks whether those in power are being ignored here.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as monarch, so those who reign are acting as rulers.

clue.text: Forcibly removes great batsman (Stokes) at end of over

indicators.note: placed at the end of another piece, these letters follow it

blocks.note: up means over, as in time's up
Joe Root is a leading England Test batsman
the initial of Ben Stokes, Root's England teammate

explanation.surface: A cricket report on two England batsmen at the end of an over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like the cricket term (six balls); here it means finished. Root and Stokes are England cricketers.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot is to pull a plant out by its roots, or to move people from home against their will.
